title: The Garden Above the Fire
subtitle: In Which Waluigi Finds The Real Luigi, Answers The Wrong Brother's Question, And Hates How Right The Feeling Was
filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — filed from the desk after the clinic report, with sulfur still in the margins
pullQuote: Luigi asked whether they were still superstars. Mario was not there. Waluigi answered anyway, and Waluigi will answer again if the archive needs to hear it louder.
standfirst: The rescue file closes the compound chase, and because Waluigi was not beside this story, Waluigi was INSIDE it, the cut cannot pretend to be distant. This is the fake Luigi coughing water, the hallway argument reported by a liar, the yellow cape, the lava moat, Kat and Ana on the rocks, Luigi burned and alive, the sentence about the star, Dr. Toad's clinic, and the line Waluigi said because silence would have been worse.

sections.heading: First We Wake The Wrong Luigi, Because Of COURSE We Do
sections.body:
Waluigi begins where the rescue file begins: with water in the wrong Luigi's face. Mona pours it, Wario looms, Ashley has the broom ready, Jimmy T cracks his knuckles, and Waluigi has the pen out before Waluigi remembers deciding to take it out. That is not a detail for decoration. That is how Waluigi knows the night has crossed from fight into filing. A weapon goes in one hand, a record goes in the other, and if the world wants Waluigi to choose, the world should stop producing suspects who wear Luigi's face like a costume bought in a hurry.

The impostor wakes tied, coughing, and trying to locate which kind of trouble he has fallen into. Answer: ALL KINDS. Wario says wake up now, which is less a sentence than a building falling on you. Mona says he has explaining to do. Ashley does not need to say anything because a witch with a broom pointed at your future is ALREADY GRAMMAR. Jimmy T supplies the little dry knuckle sound. Waluigi supplies the part history remembers.

Then the false Luigi says, *"Alright, alright... I get it. I'll talk."*

Reader, this is when Waluigi mistrusts him HARDER. A prisoner who talks before the second shove is either beaten empty or beginning the next performance. Waluigi has seen both. Waluigi has also worked around Wario's accounting office, where men will confess to anything except the invoice, so Waluigi knows the difference between fear and convenience. This man had worn enough of Luigi to make the whole scene insulting. The blue cloth from the reveal lay nearby, empty and bright. Waluigi calls it a joke nobody survived because Waluigi was THERE and nobody laughed.

So the first beat is not triumph. Waluigi did not win a confession. Waluigi bought WORDS from a liar with a bottle of water and a circle of angry friends. WAH. That is a discount price and a terrible warranty.

And YES, Waluigi sees the comedy of starting a rescue by interrogating the WRONG FACE, but comedy does not cancel the REAL PROBLEM: the wrong Luigi had answers, the real Luigi had burns, and every SECOND spent laughing was a SECOND stolen from the search.

sections.heading: The Hallway Argument Arrives In A Spy's Mouth, Which Is Disgusting But Useful
sections.body:
The impostor says the fight came before Bowser sent him to us: Mario and Luigi in the castle halls, yelling loudly enough for enemies to stop pretending they were not listening. Waluigi hates that this sounds true. Waluigi hates MOST true things delivered by people tied up outside compounds. There should be a tariff on them.

He gives us pieces, not a clean play. Mario pleading, Luigi accusing, the words tumbling over each other until they sound less like brothers and more like furniture breaking in another room. Mario says brother is not something that goes away. Luigi answers from the hurt place. The line the impostor repeats is the one the room cannot digest: *"You were never my brother."*

Waluigi would like to reject that testimony. Waluigi would like to stamp it LIAR, throw it in a drawer, and go find facts with less blood on them. But the bridge had already given Waluigi one phrase: *"Koopa worked alone."* The prisoner gives it back with a hallway around it. That is not proof of every tear he claims. Waluigi does NOT trust tears reported by a spy; spies launder tears the way merchants launder coins. But phrases leave fingerprints. A sentence repeated in the wrong mouth can be more useful than a signed confession, because a confession is trying to be believed and a sentence is often just evidence trying to escape.

And Wario is silent. WARIO. The man interrupts weather. Waluigi has heard him argue with a door after opening it successfully. But here, while the rope creaks and the fake Luigi talks about Mario still reaching and Luigi still pushing away, Wario does not cut in. Waluigi records the silence because Waluigi respects rare phenomena. Comets. Honest tax forms. Wario shutting up.

The hallway matters because it moves Mario from missing statue to missing wound. Before this, Waluigi was chasing a false brother and a lead. After this, Waluigi was chasing the shape of what the real brother heard before he ran. That is WORSE. That is BETTER evidence. Waluigi hates when both words are correct.

So Waluigi files the hallway as CONDITIONAL, not discarded. MAYBE true, MAYBE poisoned, DEFINITELY useful. That is ugly archive work: hold the shard by the sharp end, keep the blood off the labels, and do not pretend PAIN becomes false because a liar carried it.

sections.heading: The Yellow Cape Points East And Wario Grabs My Arm Like A Sensible Menace
sections.body:
Waluigi asks about the yellow-caped figure because the night has already begun circling that color like a vulture with taste. The impostor reacts too quickly. *"A yellow cape, you say?"* Yes, Waluigi says, a yellow cape. Waluigi is aware of what Waluigi said. Waluigi has excellent color recognition, especially when a color has apparently handed Luigi a note before everything caught fire.

The prisoner says he saw someone leaving the castle, saw that someone give Luigi something, and points east toward the passage under the compound where the heat breathes out in pulses. This is exactly the kind of useful answer that makes a smart person SUSPICIOUS. Wario proves he is a smart person by grabbing Waluigi's arm before Waluigi can run directly into the mouth of the clue.

*"You really believe this guy?"* Wario asks.

Waluigi wants to say no. Waluigi also wants to say MOVE. The note matters. The yellow cape matters. The prisoner knows the phrase about Koopa working alone. That means the lie is connected to the truth, and connected lies are the worst kind because they can point to real doors. Wario says the man tricked us and might be feeding us Bowser's next trap. Waluigi records, under protest, that Wario is NOT WRONG. Please do not make a plaque. Waluigi will deny approving the font.

Mona steps in because Mona has the rare gift of making urgency sound like a plan instead of panic. Ashley agrees with her eyes already on the tunnel. Jimmy T mutters something built like a curse doing stretches. The group stands on the edge of a decision: interrogate longer and lose time, or move now and possibly walk into a second trick.

Wario lets go and says, *"Let's find Luigi."*

There. That is the whole rescue turning on one ugly hinge. Waluigi does not thank the prisoner. Waluigi does not untie him. Waluigi runs. Because a lead can be bait and STILL be the only path to a dying friend. WAH. The archive should print that on hazard signs.

That is why Waluigi writes WARIO WAS RIGHT in the smallest possible letters. The lead was DANGEROUS. The delay was DANGEROUS. The only SAFE option had already died somewhere between the bridge, the axe, the note, and Luigi going over the falls.

sections.heading: The Lava Moat Has Witnesses, Because WarioWare Loyalty Is A Disease
sections.body:
The search goes to the lava moat before the east passage can swallow the whole night. Waluigi last saw Luigi near the falls, and if Luigi was alive, hurt, carried, hidden, or dead, that place had first claim on the answer. The file says the heat hit before the glow. Waluigi remembers that kind of heat: it does not warm you, it ACCUSES you. It gets in the teeth. It makes every shout sound borrowed from a larger animal.

Wario shouts Luigi's name until the word breaks apart. Mona calls too. Ashley goes higher because witches are useful in exactly the ways tall men pretend they do not envy. Waluigi will admit nothing except that she saw what ground-bound fools could not: smoke, high rocks, and two shapes waving like they had arrived at the world's least convenient balcony.

Kat and Ana. Of COURSE Kat and Ana. They followed us without permission, because WarioWare loyalty is a medical condition and apparently contagious among ninjas. Wario bellows what they are doing there. Mona rubs her temples. Waluigi saves breath for the question that matters: Did they see Luigi?

Yes. Limping but alive. Burns on arms and legs. Exhausted. Face not burned.

Waluigi did not know Waluigi had been holding breath until that last sentence gave it back. Face not burned. Alive. Not safe, not healed, not explained, but alive. Waluigi has filed kingdoms with less gratitude than Waluigi felt for those four words. Do not get sentimental. Waluigi is not sentimental. Waluigi is an ARCHIVIST under thermal stress.

Then the witnesses give the colder clue: Luigi kept repeating *"Find them."*

Find who? Mario? The yellow cape? The star? The note's sender? Waluigi does not know, and the honest sentence is always more frightening than the clever one. Kat and Ana should be reprimanded for following into a lava search. Waluigi instead files their witness statements. That is what gratitude looks like after Waluigi has sanded off the embarrassing parts. It still shines through. Annoying.

Also: if anyone asks whether Waluigi authorized two young ninjas to climb around a LAVA MOAT at NIGHT, the answer is NO, LOUD NO, OFFICIAL NO. If anyone asks whether their disobedience helped save Luigi, the answer is ALSO YES, and Waluigi resents the paperwork.

sections.heading: The Cap Is There, And Waluigi Has To Become Useful Instead Of Clever
sections.body:
Kat points. Ana runs. Jimmy T yells wait up while crossing rocks that are safe only because they are not actively molten at that second. Mona drags him through the last stretch. Ashley loops back, then ahead. Wario and Waluigi run like the tunnel owes them money, which is Wario's native gait and Waluigi's emergency imitation of it.

Then Waluigi sees the cap.

Green. Familiar. Slumped against the cavern wall above smoke. Luigi is under it, conscious but not well, burned arms wrapped in strips torn from his own shirt, face pale from heat and pain. Waluigi says conscious because Waluigi has learned to respect small victories when large ones are unavailable. Conscious is not fine. Conscious is a bridge that has not fallen yet.

Before we reach him, Luigi asks, *"Are we-a still superstars?"*

There are questions that enter a room looking for one person and cut everybody else on the way in. This one was for Mario. Waluigi knew it. Wario knew it. Mona knew it without touching him. Ashley knew it and sat quiet. Jimmy T looked down at his shoes, which is what good people do when there is no useful place for their face.

Waluigi asks about the letter because Waluigi is still Waluigi, and the archive still needs the sentence. It comes out sharper than intended: please tell me. Luigi, braced by Wario, drags the words out slowly: *"The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire."*

That is evidence, but Waluigi will not inflate it. The paper is still missing. The archive has Luigi's recalled text, not the note itself. Waluigi can hear every investigator in the future trying to polish that into certainty. NO. A burned, delirious survivor remembering a sentence is a lead, not custody. It is precious. It is incomplete. Waluigi can hold both without dropping either, because Waluigi's hands are ridiculous but competent.

The star is not lost. Fine. Waluigi writes it down. Now Waluigi would like the universe to stop hiding stars in riddles above fire.

Notice the order, because Waluigi notices order: FIRST the living body, THEN the question, THEN the note. The clue matters, but the clue did not bleed. Luigi did. Waluigi writes that down before the clever people arrive and rearrange the file around the RIDDLE.

sections.heading: Yes, We Are Still Superstars, And No, Waluigi Is Not Fine About It
sections.body:
Luigi asks again: *"We are still superstars, right?"*

Waluigi needs the reader to understand the shape of the silence. This was not ordinary nobody-knows-what-to-say silence. This was wrong-person-in-the-room silence. The correct answer belonged to Mario, and Mario was absent so completely that the cavern seemed to make room for him. Lava below. Smoke around. A brother's question hanging in air hot enough to cook excuses.

Waluigi is excellent at clever. Waluigi can insult a chandelier into dimming itself. Waluigi can turn a bad silence into a worse joke and call the movement tactics. But this was not a place for clever. Luigi was burned, frightened, and half speaking through us to someone who was not there. Mona's hand stopped short of touching him. Ashley sat close anyway. Jimmy T had no dance left in him. Wario turned away first, which is how Wario admits a thing is hurting without letting the room collect evidence. Too late. Waluigi collected it. Waluigi collects EVERYTHING.

Waluigi tells Luigi to focus on us, talk to me. Luigi whispers, *"Are we still superstars... Please come-a back to me..."*

And then Waluigi answers.

*"We are still superstars."*

The first time is barely louder than the lava. Waluigi says it again because sometimes the record needs a second nail. *"...We're still superstars."*

This is the center of the file. Not the clue, not the prisoner, not even the medical chart. THIS. Luigi asks Mario a question. Waluigi answers, not as replacement, not as theft, not as the better brother, because Waluigi is many things but Waluigi is not that kind of liar. Waluigi answers because leaving Luigi alone with silence would have been cruelty dressed up as accuracy.

A tear slips down Luigi's soot-streaked cheek and hisses on the hot stone. Waluigi would like that image to stop existing. It has refused. WAH.

And YES, Waluigi knows the sentence is simple. SIMPLE is not SMALL. SIMPLE is what remains when panic burns the decorations off the words. SUPERSTARS was the word Luigi had left. Waluigi gave it back to him before the cavern could take it too.

sections.heading: Home Is Not A Speech. Home Is Wario Carrying The Man Out
sections.body:
*"Let's go home."*

This is a small sentence doing a large job. It does not find Mario. It does not identify the yellow cape. It does not explain the garden above the fire or make the paper appear in Waluigi's glove. It gives feet a direction, and sometimes that is the only magic available to people who are not actually casting spells. Waluigi respects practical enchantments. They are harder to brag about, which makes them morally suspicious, but they WORK.

Wario lifts Luigi with care. Waluigi wants that sentence framed in iron. Wario will hate it. Excellent. Mona helps until gripping him risks the burns and then steadies from the back. Ashley scouts ahead. Kat and Ana keep to the high route where they can. Jimmy T brings up the rear, quiet now. Waluigi walks behind and watches every shadow because the fake Luigi's testimony has not magically made Bowser's compound honest. A prisoner talked. A tunnel can still answer back with teeth.

Every bend looks like another trap. Every pipe looks like a mouth. Luigi winces every few steps. Wario adjusts without being asked. Waluigi sees this. Waluigi files this. Waluigi will bring it up whenever Wario pretends his heart is only a moneybag with legs. He will say Waluigi is lying. Waluigi will point at the record. This is why records are beautiful and friendship is inconvenient.

Then the tunnel opens. Cooler air. Smoke-thinned stars. Luigi breathes like a man surfacing and says fresh air is nice. That line is small too, and Waluigi keeps it because the whole night has been enormous enough.

The question changes. It is no longer *is Luigi alive?* He is. Now it is what happened, who wrote the note, where the garden is, and how fast burns can be treated before Waluigi begins attempting medicine by glaring at injuries until they apologize. Waluigi is a gifted glarer. Waluigi is not licensed. Probably.

This is the part Waluigi likes least because it proves the crew worked: NO speech, NO parade, NO victory pose, just hands under weight and eyes on exits. Waluigi prefers victories with brass. The good ones often arrive breathing hard and saying NOTHING.

sections.heading: Dr. Toad Is Apparently His Name, And The Chart Is More Honest Than Comforting
sections.body:
Jimmy T asks about a hospital, proving again that the quiet practical question can arrive dressed as the smartest person in the room. Mona knows Star Hill has a clinic close enough to reach before the burns stiffen further. Ashley goes ahead. Wario carries Luigi on his back, and Luigi holds on with the discipline of a man trying not to scream into someone else's neck. Waluigi does not make a joke there. Waluigi is capable of restraint when the alternative is unforgivable. Mark the date.

The clinic front desk sees Wario carrying a limp Luigi and prepares to scream. Waluigi steps in front and says he is ALIVE, because apparently Waluigi must now manage medical reception. Then the doctor appears smiling: *"Dr. Toad, at your service!"*

Waluigi asks whether Doctor Toad is really his name. Waluigi stands by the question. In a night of fake Luigis and missing brothers, a physician named Dr. Toad is not automatically suspicious, but it is at least aggressively ON THEME.

Then he works, and Waluigi gives credit where credit is due. Scissors through filthy bandages. Clean water. Salve. Fresh wrapping. Luigi's face tightening when cloth lifts from a burn. Wario staring at the wall as though pain can be intimidated. Mona explaining too quickly. Ashley using the window instead of the door because apparently architecture is a suggestion.

The verdict is better than it could have been and worse than anyone wanted: serious but treatable, mostly second-degree burns on arms and legs, confusion attributed to pain, exhaustion, and trauma delirium. Fluids. Clean dressings. Two weeks of rest. Absolutely no adventuring.

Luigi winces harder at that than at some bandages, because heroes are idiots and Waluigi is apparently surrounded by them professionally. Dr. Toad writes the chart anyway. Good. The chart is an exhibit because the archive needs paper that does not flinch. Waluigi can flinch for it. Quietly. In another room. Maybe.

The clinic does not solve the mystery, and Waluigi refuses to let the clean bandages trick the reader. MEDICAL STABLE is not SAFE. TREATABLE is not ANSWERED. Rest is not resolution. It is merely the floor Luigi needed under him before the next question could stand.

sections.heading: The Arc Ends Here, Which Is Not The Same As Everything Being Fine
sections.body:
Then Dr. Toad asks why Luigi was at the castle alone. Does he not usually travel with his brother?

Every bottle in the room seems to stop clinking. Waluigi knows that is not literal; Waluigi also knows the archive is allowed ONE dramatic sensory truth when the question deserves it. Luigi looks at Waluigi, then at the sheets, and says they had an argument. He left on his own. The doctor apologizes himself out of the room, which proves he may be named Dr. Toad but he has survival instincts.

Ashley gives space. Mona stays close enough to help and far enough not to corner anyone. Wario leans against the wall with arms crossed, which is Wario for I am emotionally present and I HATE that you can tell. Waluigi stands at the window deciding whether to say Mario's name. Not yet. That is the important part. Waluigi, who says almost everything too early, does not say it. Luigi is burned, bandaged, and still speaking through absence. A file can wait. A wound cannot.

Waluigi admits he is not great at this. Luigi laughs, short and broken by pain: of course not, you are my rival after all. Waluigi almost smiles. Wario sees it because Wario detects weakness with the accuracy of a rat detecting kitchens. Then Wario gives the line the file earns: Mario is gone, everyone knows it, that does not mean Luigi has to be stupid about it. You two are both idiots, but you are better than this.

Waluigi could object to the idiot classification. Waluigi chooses not to, because sometimes accuracy arrives wearing muddy boots and you let it sit down.

So yes: the arc ends here. Rescue objective resolved. Luigi found alive. Clinic reached. The false Luigi remains unnamed, the paper remains unrecovered, the yellow cape remains loose, and Mario remains absent. That is not continuation of the SAME chase. That is the next door. The current door closes with Luigi breathing in a clinic bed and Waluigi having said the sentence Mario was not there to say.

We are still superstars. Waluigi has filed it. Waluigi means it. WAH.

And if the next arc tries to pretend this one never hurt, Waluigi will THROW THE FILE at it. The closure is REAL. The damage is REAL. The lead is OPEN. The brother is ABSENT. All four statements fit in the same room, unfortunately, because Waluigi checked.
